references.text: God's promise to Abraham to give the land to his descendants, fulfilled in Exodus 6:8.
God's covenant with Abraham where He promises to give the land from the River of Egypt to the Euphrates to his offspring.
God confirms the promise to Isaac to give him and his descendants these lands.
God repeats the promise to Jacob to give him and his offspring the land he is lying on.
Joseph reminds them of God's oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to bring them out of Egypt to the promised land.
God's declaration to lead the Israelites out of Egypt into a good and spacious land.
The promise that the Lord will lead the people into the land of the Canaanites as He swore to their fathers.
Reference to the land which God raised His hand and swore to let them dwell in.
The Lord commanded Israel to go in and take the land He swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God shows Moses the land He swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God reminds that He raised His hand and swore to bring Israel out of Egypt to a land flowing with milk and honey.
God promises to bring Israel back to the land He swore to give to their fathers.
Reference to God's promise and oath to Abraham, showing how God confirms His promises with an oath.
Abraham obeyed in faith when he was called to go out to a land he would receive as an inheritance.
Ezekiel 47:14 confirms that the division of the land as an inheritance rests on the same 'raised hand' oath as in Exodus 6:8.
Exodus 33:1 links the deliverance directly to the same oath made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as in Exodus 6:8.
Ezekiel 20:5 provides the historical context for when and how God's oath with a 'raised hand' was given in Egypt.
Exodus 32:13 confirms that the promise of the land was given by oath and shows how this promise is used as a basis for prayer.
